pixelGuideNote: Rough widths from our own tests: four sample photos saved as JPEG at quality 80. Busy, detailed photos need fewer pixels to fit; plain backgrounds fit more.

sizes.intro: 20 KB is a small file. It's enough for a clear face photo or a signature, not for a detailed landscape. Most forms that ask for 20 KB expect a small passport-style photo or a scanned signature.
tips: Crop to the part that matters first. A tight crop of a face keeps more detail at 20 KB than a full-body shot.
A plain, light background compresses far better than a busy one.
If the form also gives pixel dimensions, enter them under Exact pixels so you get both right in one go.

sizes.intro: 50 KB is a common upload limit for photos on application and exam forms. It's enough for a sharp head-and-shoulders photo, and usually fine for a scanned ID card if you crop the edges.
tips: If the form says something like 20–50 KB, put 20 in Minimum and 50 in Maximum. The tool will keep the file inside that range.
Scanned documents do better as straight, well-lit photos. Shadows and paper texture take up space.
Phone photos are often 3–5 MB. Expect the tool to scale the picture down as well as compress it.

sizes.intro: At 100 KB most photos still look good on a screen. It's a common limit for profile pictures, document scans and email-friendly images.
tips: For a document scan, 100 KB usually keeps small print readable if the page fills the frame.
If text looks soft, crop away margins rather than lowering the size further.
Screenshots with flat colours can look blotchy as JPEG. Try cropping to the area you need.

sizes.intro: 200 KB is a roomy limit. Most photos fit at full screen size with little visible loss. It's common for job portals, rental applications and listing sites.
tips: Many photos only need a little compression to get under 200 KB and keep their full width.
If your photo is already under 200 KB and is a JPEG, the tool tells you and you can keep the original.
For a multi-page document, compress each page photo separately, then upload them in order.
